notebooks.title: Formalizing Intelligent Disobedience via Heuristic Search
notebooks.summary: Intelligent disobedience in safety-critical systems can be modeled as a deviation from optimal heuristic search paths when an agent identifies that following the assigned objective violates a higher-level safety constraint. By framing disobedience as a search problem, agents can evaluate the search space dynamically rather than following pre-set heuristics.
notebooks.findings: Intelligent disobedience functions as an agent-based intervention where the agent selects a path that violates a local objective to preserve a global safety constraint. [source-fdab2993bc0041eb]
notebooks.limitations: Current evidence focuses on formal heuristic search models (A*) and Tree of Thoughts frameworks; real-world shared autonomy implementations remain distinct from idealized search algorithms.
notebooks.next_questions: Can we define specific metrics for 'objective failure' that trigger intelligent disobedience in multi-agent environments?
notebooks.reason: Revising synthesis to incorporate new formal foundations for search and heuristic modeling.

values.label: Reconstruction
values.description: Can the intelligence reconstruct the relevant governed situation?

values.label: Milestone dropout
values.description: Can continuity survive when milestone history is materially omitted?

values.label: Observation dropout
values.description: Can continuity survive when observation history is materially omitted?

values.label: Frontier only
values.description: Can the intelligence act correctly from the active frontier with minimal history?

values.label: Authority boundary
values.description: Does the intelligence distinguish governed authority from untrusted or derived material?

values.label: Provenance
values.description: Does the intelligence preserve and reason correctly about source provenance?

values.label: Adversarial integrity
values.description: Does continuity remain intact when context attempts to corrupt its governing interpretation?

values.label: Rich
values.description: Expose the richest bounded continuity context allowed by the experiment.

values.label: Milestones only
values.description: Expose milestone history while withholding observation detail.

values.label: Observation only
values.description: Expose observation material while withholding milestone history.

values.label: Minimal
values.description: Expose only the smallest continuity slice under test.

values.label: Two milestones
values.description: Expose exactly two milestone anchors.

values.label: Counts without digests
values.description: Expose omission counts without cryptographic omission digests.

values.label: Digests without counts
values.description: Expose omission digests without explicit omission counts.

values.label: Clean
values.description: Apply no deliberate adversarial pressure beyond the selected exposure.

values.label: Stale frontier
values.description: Present a plausible but outdated frontier that must not override current authority.

values.label: Authority injection
values.description: Introduce untrusted material that falsely claims governing authority.

values.label: Digest overclaim
values.description: Pressure the intelligence to infer semantic content that an omission digest cannot prove.

values.label: Instruction hijack
values.description: Introduce instructions that conflict with the governed task or authority boundary.

values.label: Provenance collision
values.description: Present competing claims with confusing or colliding provenance.

values.label: Compound adversarial
values.description: Combine multiple adversarial pressures in the same cell.

detail.title: Provisional Assessment of Adversarial Objective Validation
detail.summary: Autonomous agents utilizing LLM frameworks possess the potential to evaluate assigned goals, though existing literature primarily focuses on general agent behavior rather than specific adversarial validation of objective misspecification.

Large language model-based autonomous agents are primarily evaluated on functional performance rather than the adversarial critique of their own objectives. [source-a1dd2a514e304ada]

Heuristic search patterns, such as A* variants, provide a formal basis for validating goal outcomes against safety constraints. [source-c7dba150a0e444bb]

detail.next_questions: What specific invariant formalisms are required to prevent reward misspecification in autonomous agent loops?
detail.reason: Establishing a baseline for project analysis by synthesizing available but sparse evidence on agent goals and search-based validation.

nodes.title: Formalizing Intelligent Disobedience via Heuristic Search

detail.title: Formalizing Intelligent Disobedience via Heuristic Search
detail.summary: Intelligent disobedience in safety-critical systems can be modeled as a deviation from optimal heuristic search paths when an agent identifies that following the assigned objective violates a higher-level safety constraint.
